Readable status output with explicit current workflow state and explicit blocked/approval state.

A useful failure reason is surfaced to the user.
No silent bypasses of workflow controls.
Non-interactive operation where appropriate.
requirements.verification: test: commands never block on stdin (vague — see prd-issues)

requirements.requirement: No orphaned runtime processes where supported cleanup is available.
requirements.verification: test: process table clean after run

requirements.requirement: No indefinite waits on external agent processes.
No accidental repeated publishing.
No duplicate initialization damage.
Ability to resume/recover from persisted workflow state.
Browser automation is not a mandatory verification mechanism in the core release.
requirements.verification: code inspection: no browser dependency in core verification

requirements.requirement: No unlimited autonomous agent loops.
No claims of support for multiple agents before their adapters exist.
requirements.verification: code inspection: docs claims vs adapters

requirements.requirement: A stable agent adapter interface lets additional runtimes integrate without changing the core state machine; adapters cannot own transitions or self-approve, and must use structured transport, bounded execution, capability probing, controlled permissions, repository/configuration boundary protection, a compatible response protocol, and deterministic error handling.
requirements.verification: code inspection + adapter contract tests (not required for current baseline)

requirements.requirement: An optional Claude Code adapter implements the same workflow contract with no Claude-specific behavior in the core orchestrator, preserving approvals, deterministic verification, workspace isolation, environment restrictions, evidence freshness, and protected publishing.
An optional Codex adapter uses the same workflow contracts; Codex execution stays subordinate to the state machine, verification gates, approval records, and Git publisher.
An optional Freebuff adapter must not revive a second orchestration system or relax the core security model.

Logical workflow roles (analyst/griller, spec/planner, implementation, code reviewer, verifier/reviewer, fixer, security reviewer) remain stable across runtimes and may map onto a small number of physical permission profiles.
Multi-agent parallelism must not weaken approval ordering, state consistency, workspace integrity, evidence binding, or deterministic gate behavior.
Alternative workspace providers (containers, remote workspaces, other backends) must satisfy the baseline/lease/scope/integrity contract.
Runtime verification extensions beyond HTTP remain explicit and deterministic; browser automation only as an optional adapter meeting the same evidence/security requirements.
External security audit tools/skills are advisory/audit inputs, read-only, never granted permission to alter the repository, and their findings enter gates only if explicitly integrated.
All future integrations plug into the current workflow rather than replacing it.

A change altering workflow safety, approval semantics, state transitions, evidence semantics, or publishing authority requires an explicit versioned product decision, not a silent adapter-level change.
A developer can obtain the product and understand how to use it without reading the implementation source first.

Implementation-vs-PRD conflicts are resolved using the §42 priority order: human approval authority, deterministic verification, evidence/approval freshness and integrity, workspace/configuration boundaries, safe Git publishing, smallest implementation, explicit extensions.
